_why: The min_class_size=10 floor deletes 32 classes and 121 rows. Deleting is the
right call for the *label* - a class with 2 examples cannot be predicted - but
it is not obviously the right call for the *pixels*. A Lip Gloss tile is a
photograph of a lipstick-shaped object on white, and the model has only 15
Lipstick tiles to learn that shape from.
So instead of deleting the row, relabel it to the nearest KEPT class. The test
applied to every candidate below is deliberately strict: would a person
shown the two products at 60x80 struggle to tell them apart, or is one
literally a subtype of the other? Where the answer is no, the class stays
dropped - a merge that is merely same-family is how Task 3's catch-all 'Other'
class ended up with F1 = 0.000.
This is why 'Blazers -> Tshirts' is absent even though both are Topwear, and
why Umbrellas, Wristbands, Cushion Covers, Ipad, Key chain, Body Wash and
Scrub and Eyeshadow are absent entirely: they have no kept sibling that looks
anything like them.
The payoff concentrates exactly where the graded submission needs it:
Lipstick 15 -> 25 rows (+67%), Foundation and Primer 12 -> 22 (+83%). Those
two classes carry 6.9% of the deliverable between them.
Rows merged this way are scored under their NEW label in val and test, so any
run using this map must be labelled as a variant and never compared silently
against a run that does not.

Lip Gloss.why: same product form factor - a small cylindrical tube shot upright on white

Lip Plumper.why: same tube form factor; the difference is the formulation, not the picture

Compact.why: flat round face-base product; indistinguishable from a pressed foundation at 60x80

Concealer.why: face-base product in the same tube/wand packaging

Highlighter and Blush.why: pressed face powder in the same compact packaging

Shoe Laces.why: literally a member of the target class

Ties and Cufflinks.why: literally a superset naming of the target class

Blazers.why: structured long-sleeved outerwear, front-opening; the same silhouette

Nehru Jackets.why: a jacket subtype; differs by collar, which 60x80 does not resolve

Rain Jacket.why: a jacket subtype; differs by fabric, not by shape

Tights.why: same garment silhouette; the distinction is denier, invisible at this size

Rain Trousers.why: loose technical trouser with an elasticated waist - the same outline

Lounge Tshirts.why: a t-shirt; the label records where it is worn, not what it looks like

Robe.why: long loose nightwear garment shot flat

Baby Dolls.why: short nightwear dress; the same category of garment

Trolley Bag.why: large soft-sided travel bag - nearest kept luggage class

Tablet Sleeve.why: flat padded device carrier; differs only in size, which a tile does not convey

Footballs.why: spherical sports ball on white; nearest kept class in Sports Equipment

Hat.why: brimmed headwear; nearest kept class in Headwear

Clothing Set.why: multi-piece outfit photographed together; the only kept Apparel Set class

still_dropped._why: no kept sibling that resembles them - merging would repeat Task 3's 'Other' mistake
